chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from some of his narrators, from Dawud al-Riqqi, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) said: Shall I not inform you of the true jurist? They said: Sure, O Commander of the Believers. He said: The one who does not make the people despair from the mercy of Allah, nor puts them at safety from the torment of Allah, nor gives them license to acts of disobedience to Allah, nor abandons the Qur'an out of desire away from it to others. Alas, there is no good in knowledge in which there is no understanding. Alas, there is no good in reading in which there is no contemplation. Alas, there is no good in worship in which there is no comprehension.

key_terms.الفقيه: The jurist, a scholar of Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What are the defining characteristics of a true jurist (faqih) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Mani al-Akhbar*, establishes the theological and practical criteria for a true *faqih*, emphasizing the balance between hope (*raja'*) and fear (*khauf*) to prevent spiritual despair or complacency. It underscores that authentic religious authority requires not just ritual observance but deep contemplation (*tadabbur*) of the Qur'an and jurisprudential insight (*tafaqquh*), ensuring the jurist guides the community accurately without granting undue license for sins.
